title: Kth Smallest Number in Multiplication Table
description:
Consider an `m x n` multiplication table (1-indexed) where the cell at row `i` and column `j` holds the value `i * j` (`1 <= i <= m`, `1 <= j <= n`).

Given integers `m`, `n`, and `k`, return the `k`-th smallest integer in this `m x n` multiplication table (counting duplicates with multiplicity).
hints: Binary search the answer value x in [1, m * n] rather than building the matrix.
For any candidate x, row i (which holds i, 2i, ..., n*i) contributes min(x // i, n) values <= x; sum this across all rows to check whether count(x) >= k.

examples.explanation: The 3x3 multiplication table sorted is [1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 6, 6, 9]; the 5th smallest element is 3.
The 2x3 multiplication table sorted is [1, 2, 2, 3, 4, 6]; the 6th smallest element is 6.
The 1st smallest element in any multiplication table is always 1.
